chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Little Harlem in Buffalo: the on-air battle with Stuff Smith
summary: A small band grew to seven with John L. Henderson and Joe Thomas; on a radio half hour they battled Stuff Smith's band three blocks away at Little Harlem, and each copied the other's arrangements.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well, listen, now let me take you back to where we were. Luke sent for you.
Yeah, then Luke got them to --
And Joe Thomas came in too.
And I worked there for awhile. We were five pieces in there. They had four rhythm and myself, and then in come John L. Henderson on alto, and Joe Thomas on the tenor.
Yeah, so then you had seven.
Then we had seven, and we got to swinging in there pretty good, and we had a little battle of music, where Stuff had a band which was about three blocks away.

This club was owned by a woman by the name of Ann Montgomery. And he had a band in there, and we used to get there and they had this Round the Town broadcast, and whatever -- and we'd get to battling on that, you know. We had a half hour, so we'd stretch out.
Oh, on the air, a battle on the air?
Yeah, to make it hard. We'd study up things to play, arrangements, so we could sound better than

Stuff. And then sometimes Stuff would be listening to us, when we'd play, and then he'd change his whole radio program. He'd say, "Those guys feel good tonight. We're going to change the whole program and open up with 'Ring Them Bells', or something like that." You know. And once we caught them. They come over in the daytime, and was copying our arrangements, you know, and they would play them in front of us. If they would go on first, they would play them, and we'd have to change our whole thing around, you know. Oh, it was fun in music then, you know, it was great fun.
